points.description: Correctly distinguishes the two modes: asynchronous sends each character individually, framed by a start bit and a stop bit (simple/cheap, low transmission rate); synchronous groups several characters into a continuous stream/frames delimited by SYN or flag (more complex, higher rate), with synchronization between sender and receiver.
points.partial_credit: Award half if only one mode is described correctly, or both are given but the contrast (character-wise with start/stop bits vs. frame/block-wise with higher rate) is incomplete.

rubric.notes: Full marks for a correct contrast of both modes: per-character start/stop bits, simple, low rate versus continuous frames delimited by SYN/flag, more complex, higher rate, with sender-receiver synchronization. Half for describing only one mode correctly or a partial contrast. Equivalent wording is accepted.
